Changes in patchset 23:

- Removed all strcmp calls and replaced the original event classification mechanism with a switch-case structure based on the EventType enum.

- Added DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault for CPU_THERMAL_TRIP and FAST_PROCHOT_ASSERTION events.

- Added PowerRailFault for HSC_OCP, P12V_STBY_UV, POWER_ON_SEQUENCE_FAILURE, and DIMM_PMIC_ERROR events.
Patchset 24: Use a consistent approach for sdbusplus namespaces.

Could we create a JSON file for different platforms to overwrite components?

@amithash@meta.com What do you think about solving the component problem across different platforms?

In a perfect world, these should be retrieved from the BIC. So, if we have for example, a ARM server controller vs an AMD server controller, I suspect the names of these VRs would change. IMHO this is what PDRs were supposed to address.

To be honest, I see OEM as a temporary measure while we figure out the story on how we can better utilize more standard interfaces. So, it could be a couple of platforms stuck on the OEM variants while our future platforms jump onto other more standard PLDM features?
Maybe we can make that kind of improvement in the future, I think the current version should be merged first.

Hi @rushtotom@gmail.com, @deepak.kodihalli.83@gmail.com, @manojkiran.eda@gmail.com, @amithash@meta.com,

Could you please help review this commits?

Thanks
Why are we calling logging-create directly here??
Currently, there are no logging interfaces for this kind of event. Do you have any suggestions on how to handle it?
Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz, another reason for directly calling logging-create is to have control over the severity of the logged event. Please let me know if this approach doesn’t work for you.

> Currently, there are no logging interfaces for this kind of event. Do you have any suggestions on how to handle it?  

I don't know what the event is.  All I see here is a string shoved in to phosphor-logging.  Whatever it is, we probably need to define an event in phosphor-dbus-interfaces?

> another reason for directly calling logging-create is to have control over the severity of the logged event.

Different severity should be different events.

If you’d like us to refine the patch thoroughly before merging, we can certainly do that. I completely agree that all events should be recorded in a structured manner. 

The event system in our machine carries a lot of historical baggage, as you mentioned, many components have simply “shoved the human-readable string into phosphor-logging.” 

Refactoring everything to fully utilize the event definitions in phosphor-dbus-interfaces would take quite a long time. 

Our primary consideration is that there are currently several tickets depending on this patch. I’d prefer to merge the current version first and handle the enhancements later.
Can we split the handling of this particular error into a separate commit then?  There shouldn't be anyone at Meta relying on a raw Logging.Create call.
Done
Please don't add FUNC.  phosphor-logging already includes this information in the messages.
Done
I'd prefer not to log it into the journal and in phosphor-logging.
Do you mean removing all lg2::info and lg2::error? I think it’s convenient to keep them for our testing, and lg2::commit logs into the journal as well.

All I mean is:

If we are calling lg2::commit (or similar) we don't need a lg2::error or lg2::info _also_.
